headline: Profit rebounds on easier comps as margins slip
summary_short: Ingersoll Rand reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2,048.8 million (+8.5% y/y, +10.9% q/q) and swung to net income of $256.8 million ($0.66 diluted EPS), versus a $115.3 million net loss a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 8.5% y/y (+10.9% q/q) to $2,048.8M; organic growth was 4.1%, with the rest from M&A and FX. GAAP net income swung to $256.8M ($0.66/diluted share) from a $115.3M loss a year ago, which had included a $266M goodwill/intangible impairment and a $121M equity-method loss. On an adjusted basis, EBITDA rose just 2% to $519.9M as margin fell 160bp to 25.4% on China pricing/inflation pressure; Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.86 (+7% y/y). Free cash flow was $268.9M. Ingersoll Rand updated FY2026 guidance to revenue growth of 4.5%-6.5%, Adjusted EBITDA of $2,130-2,190M, and Adjusted EPS of $3.45-3.57 (expected near the high end). Cash fell 10.5% y/y to $1,173.5M; short-term debt rose to $699.8M from $2.0M.

The shard's 'ebitda_usd_m' metric ($523.2M) is a Yahoo-derived GAAP-basis EBITDA proxy and is not the same measure as the company's own 'Adjusted EBITDA' ($519.9M, +2% y/y) disclosed in the release -- the two are close this quarter by coincidence and should not be treated as interchangeable across periods. The release states it is 'updating' full-year 2026 guidance but never uses 'raised'/'lowered'/'reaffirmed' language for the consolidated ranges, so guidance move is recorded as null rather than assumed raised, despite Adjusted EPS being 'expected to finish near the high end' of its range.

drivers.explanation: Reported revenue growth of 8.5% y/y was ~4.1 points organic (IT&S +4% organic revenue, P&ST +4% organic revenue/+7% organic orders), ~2.8 points from M&A, and ~1.6 points from FX.
The swing versus a $76.4M prior-year base is largely a comp effect: Q2 2025 included a $229.7M goodwill impairment and a $36.1M intangible impairment absent this quarter.
Swing to profit reflects the same prior-year impairments plus a $120.9M loss on equity-method investments in Q2 2025 that did not recur.
Cash declined as the company deployed $110M to M&A (including Fox s.r.l.) and returned $248M to shareholders ($240M buybacks, $8M dividends) during the quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA grew just 2% and margin fell 160bp to 25.4%, which management attributed to inflationary cost pressure it could not fully offset with price, primarily in China.

Ingersoll Rand updated full-year 2026 guidance to revenue growth of 4.5%-6.5%, Adjusted EBITDA of $2,130-2,190M, and Adjusted EPS of $3.45-3.57, expecting to finish near the high end of the EPS range.
